snippet.title: He tricked the prime minister of UAE 💀
snippet.description:
Omar Al Olama shares an unbelievable phone-call story with Nikhil Kamath.
It starts with a mysterious call.
Omar says he received a phone call from someone who told him, “We have a few questions to ask you,” before abruptly hanging up.
Because Omar had previously worked in the Telecom Regulations Authority, he understood how IP phones were used in many offices. He explains that changing the last two digits of an IP phone number to 00 or 99 could make the call reach reception.
So Omar decided to test it.
He called the number again with 99 at the end.
Someone answered.
And then he heard:
“Prime Minister’s Office, can I help you?”
What makes the story fascinating is how quickly an ordinary phone call turned into something completely unexpected. Omar recognized a technical pattern because of his previous experience, tested it himself, and ended up reaching the Prime Minister’s Office.
This is a great example of how understanding the systems around you can sometimes reveal possibilities that most people would never think to try.
Would you have had the confidence to try the 99 trick?

snippet.title: Bengaluru is living in 2070
snippet.description:
During his visit to the Bengaluru Traffic Police headquarters, Nikhil Kamath hears M.N. Anucheth explain how Bengaluru is using AI-based traffic signals to manage congestion.

The system uses computer vision to understand the traffic load at each arm of a junction and optimize signal timing accordingly. If there are no vehicles at a junction, the system can avoid giving unnecessary timing to that direction.

According to Anucheth, the AI-based system has been implemented at 165 junctions across Bengaluru, and the city has seen a significant reduction in waiting time.

He also says manual signalling has come down from around 40% to 5%.

Is Bengaluru showing what the future of urban traffic management could look like?

The clip raises a broader question about traffic enforcement, accountability, and whether the same rules apply to everyone on the road.

Buying the DJI Pocket 4P in the US is currently difficult because of FCC regulations and limited availability. If you’ve been searching for where to buy the DJI Pocket 4P in the USA, you’ve probably already seen prices well above retail.

The DJI Pocket 4P Vlog Combo is supposed to retail for around $699, but many US listings have been showing up closer to $900, $1,000, or even more.

In this video, I break down my experience trying to buy and import the DJI Pocket 4P through Amazon Germany. I wanted to find out if there was a legitimate way to get the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P in the United States without paying a massive reseller markup.

I was ultimately able to order the DJI Pocket 4P Vlog Combo through Amazon for about $720, plus roughly $21 in shipping, and it arrived in the United States in about a week. The interesting part is that the order was fulfilled through Amazon Germany even though I found it while searching on the US Amazon website. By the time I checked again, though, that particular listing had already disappeared.  

Availability seems to be changing quickly, and importing the DJI Pocket 4P can also come with unexpected checkout, shipping, inventory, or regional issues. So if you’re looking for DJI Pocket 4P US stock, DJI Pocket 4P Amazon listings, or simply trying to figure out how to buy the DJI Pocket 4 in the USA, make sure you carefully check the seller, total price, shipping details, return policy, and warranty situation before ordering.
